subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation for Acme Payments

Hi Samir / Jill —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call + proposed next steps so we have alignment. I focused this recap on reliability / graceful degradation as that came up as a top priority.

Key pain points you called out:
- Recent incidents: multi-minute latency spikes during peak batch jobs (last incident 2026-07-28) and a failover that took ~14 minutes between regions.
- No standardized fallback model: teams currently route to a single in-house LLM and fall back to CPU-based heuristics when overloaded.
- Lack of fine-grained SLOs: monitoring is ad-hoc and customers surface outages before internal alerts.

Current stack you described:
- In-house model served on a mixed GPU pool (NVIDIA A100 + some older cards)
- Primary region: us-west-2; DR region: us-east-1 with manual failover
- Orchestration: custom K8s operators + sidecar caching layer
- Observability: Datadog for infra, custom app alerts with PagerDuty

Success criteria you called out (what 'good' looks like):
- P95 latency for interactive paths < 200ms under normal load
- 99.9% availability for inference endpoints on a monthly basis
- Automatic graceful degradation: when model capacity constrained, degrade to a smaller model (or cached responses) rather than timing out
- Region-level automatic failover within 2 minutes with minimal error surface to customers

Suggested Redwood approach (high level):
- Dedicated fallback model family configured per route (e.g., large -> medium -> small) with automatic routing policies and weighted canary rollouts
- Region-aware routing + health checks so requests automatically fail over to healthy region pools
- Prefix/KV caching and short-circuit cached responses for known high-traffic prompts
- SLOs and monitoring templates we can share (see attached Redwood-SLOs-v1.pdf)

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Share incident timeline & logs (you mentioned a postmortem for 2026-07-28) — Samir to send by EOD Wed (8/11).
2) Technical deep dive (1h) with your infra and our serving runtime team — propose Thu 8/12 10:00 AM PT or Fri 8/13 9:00 AM PT.
3) Draft mutual action plan (attached) and then iterate.

Could you confirm the incident postmortem availability and which time works for the deep dive? If you prefer, we can also do a short ops-only sync first (30m) to cover failover requirements.

Thanks again — I'll loop in our runtime lead if you confirm the deep dive time so we can dig into TLS, routing, and SLOs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood-SLOs-v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Torres <jill.torres@acmepayments.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation for Acme Payments

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications and additional context: 

Incident history (high level):
- 2026-07-28: peak batch + promo traffic caused a cascade where our autoscaler undershot GPU needs. Root cause is still in the postmortem but symptoms were CPU-bound control plane and model queuing.
- 2026-05-14: single-zone hardware failure; manual failover worked but was ~14 minutes to fully route traffic to us-east-1.

Fallback expectations: we want graceful degradation rather than hard failures. Ideally:
1) Prefer a smaller GPU-backed model (same family) as first fallback
2) If GPU capacity unavailable, fallback to CPU-quantized model for read-only, low-cost responses (we accept quality drop for availability)
3) If neither available, return a cached or templated message to the end user

SLOs: we think the 99.9% monthly availability target is reasonable to start. We have internal SLA obligations to merchants that make anything below 99.8% cause remediation.

Attachments I will send: the 7/28 postmortem (PDF) and our traffic heatmap for the week of 7/25-7/31. You can expect those by Wednesday EOD.

Deep dive: Thu 8/12 10:00 AM PT works for our infra + platform engineers. Please send calendar invite.

--Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Payments
samir.khan@acmepayments.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation for Acme Payments

Marissa / Jonas —

Quick internal notes after reading the thread and Samir's incident summary (high level):
- We should propose an explicit fallback graph per route: model-large -> model-medium (quantized) -> cached templated response. That maps well to their acceptance of quality drop for availability.
- Autoscaler tuning: suggest aggressive scale-up thresholds for batch windows and a small warm pool of on-demand GPUs in primary region to reduce cold-start queuing.
- Failover SLA: we can target automatic region failover in <2 minutes if we provision health-check and warm-pool cross-region. Need to validate cross-region KV cache consistency implications.
- Ask runbook/ops: request their current playbook for failover steps -- this will help us size the warm pools and canary strategy.

For the deep dive tomorrow, I'll bring a short diagram: routing policy + fallback model graph + cache short-circuit idea. Jonas, can you sketch the quantization/CPU fallback perf numbers to share?

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

What we'll bring to the deep dive (Thu 8/12 10:00 AM PT):
- Ben: routing & fallback graph + autoscaler recommendations and warm-pool sizing
- Jonas: perf numbers for quantized CPU fallbacks and expected latency/quality tradeoffs
- Runtime engineer: region failover design and KV cache consistency tradeoffs
- I'll bring a draft mutual action plan and SLO template (attached) to accelerate contracting.

Action items for Acme (Samir / Jill):
- Send 7/28 postmortem + traffic heatmap (Samir) -- target: EOD Wed 8/11 (received).
- Identify ops contact for runbook and DR steps -- please share by EOD Thu 8/12.

Tentative timeline after deep dive:
- Week 1: confirm fallback graph and sizing + MoS for SLOs
- Week 2-3: PoC in a single route (canary) with canary metrics and rollback policies
- Month 1-2: expand to critical routes + SLA negotiation

I've attached the mutual action plan and SLO playbook for your review before the call. I’ll send the calendar invite now. Looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
